beats.name: hook
beats.said: Clerk scans a ticket, sees a million-dollar win, and tells the customer it is not a winner.
beats.shown: Kyle behind the counter, push-in to the scanner and ticket, shocked face, then a deadpan face.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: The customer shrugs and leaves; the clerk fishes the ticket from the trash and pockets it.
beats.shown: Customer in green hat, trash can, dark vignette close-up, wallet, smug smile.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: That night he imagines a boat, a mansion and new friends.
beats.shown: Moonlit yacht scene with fireworks, then a shape-wipe into Kyle in bed with a bowl of the dream.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Next morning he drives two hours to the lottery office and hands over the ticket; the clerk is delighted.
beats.shown: Sunset drive in a red car, prize-claims counter, curly-haired clerk with glasses.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: He waits; the store customer walks in wearing a suit and badge with two police officers.
beats.shown: Yellow Our Winners waiting room, Kyle seated grinning, figures appear at the door.

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Lotteries noticed clerks winning far more often than others, which looked suspicious.
beats.shown: Top-down evidence board with pinned winner photos and an 'everyone else' label.

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: So they printed bait winning tickets and sent undercover agents into stores as ordinary customers.
beats.shown: Top-down ticket dispenser, agent hat, bait-and-gas shop front, return to opening shop with agent at counter.

hook.first_frame: Wide-ish view of a lottery counter; Kyle in a red shirt stands behind the till under a green hanging lamp, deadpan face looking at camera.
hook.first_3s: Slow push-in, then a fast fly-in to the scanner and ticket, then back to Kyle whose face turns to shock with sweat drop and a $1,000,000 display.
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title asks why cashiers keep winning; first line shows a cashier doing a dodgy thing with a winning ticket, answering by example rather than restating the title.

story.structure: act first, explain at the end
story.real_fact_core: Lotteries noticed clerks winning suspiciously often and now run sting operations with bait tickets and undercover agents.
story.authority_or_antagonist: Undercover lottery agent plus two police officers

tone.humour: Dry, absurd escalation: fishing from the trash, yacht daydream, grinning while waiting for his payout.
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Heavy irony: the clerk lies and is smug, then walks into his own trap; deadpan faces on the customer.
tone.dialogue_style: Short quoted lines inside narration by a single voice; no separate voices.

generation_evidence.observation: The shop interior in the last frames matches frame 0 down to lamp, board, and counter layout; the set is reused as a fixed asset.
Clerk's glasses, curls, necklace, and pencil stay rigid across the frames; only the mouth shape swaps.
Tiny pinned photo labels and 'EVERYONE ELSE' stay crisp and consistent as the camera pushes in on the board.
Boat scene is wrapped as a flat panel into a bowl, a deliberate designed transition with clean geometry.
Seated Kyle with fixed grin and constant geometry over 25 frames; only slight arm shift.
Low-poly faceted hat and bugs have simple clean shapes with painterly blur, not AI texture swim.
